correctness.rationale: The coordinate model in Q(sqrt5) is explicit and exact. The executable certificate verifies the 20 triangular and 12 pentagonal supporting facets (including all inequalities and incidences), the sixty-edge graph, all fifteen reflection symmetries, all 105 mirror-pair intersections and the 31 projective axes with their 2/3/5-fold multiplicities. Section vertices are strict crossed edges plus on-plane vertices; the potential whole-edge cases are explicitly handled by inherited endpoints. Chamber transitivity yields 12 vertices for every generic plane from one exact representative; central symmetry and vertex degree four imply 10 for every regular wall point. Every exceptional direction is among the exhaustively evaluated 31 axes, with counts 8/6/10. Euler counting gives 120 chambers. No simulation is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Direct published-research searches, semantic database comparisons and available earlier section-claim records identified no complete icosidodecahedral central-section sidedness law. The classical fifteen reflection circles, their 120 chambers, six central decagonal equators and ten hexagonal diagonal equators are explicitly excluded from novelty. Padrol--Pfeifle concerns section representation complexity; Baez describes rectification; Liu explicitly discusses two types of equators but does not label the 15-mirror normal strata. This is originality relative to inspected evidence, with nonzero residual historical priority risk.
residual_risks: Older polyhedral-section diagrams or exhaustive Coxeter polytope handbooks may encode the entire classification without searchable wording.
Full Yoshinaga 2019 article was not separately inspected; Liu provides a full account of its differently structured arrangement, but direct priority checking there remains incomplete.
The reflection chamber arrangement, six central decagonal equators and ten hexagonal special equators were previously known; no novelty attributed to those components.
Semantic and keyword search, including published-finding corpus, cannot prove global novelty or independence.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification for all central sections of the canonical rectification of the icosahedron. Unlike an arbitrary slice or a mere numerical invariant, it finds a rigid generic 12-sided section and describes all singular 10/8/6-sided exceptions by a meaningful Coxeter reflection stratification, with exact orbit sizes, chamber count and Haar almost-sure law. The complete degeneracy classification and the 15 twofold octagonal cuts go beyond the previously documented specific hexagonal/decagonal equators. It is an independently useful geometric classification, with limits restricted to central cuts and no exaggerated downstream claims.
